questions.question: A ______ happens in chess when a player gives up material during the initiation to seek some kind of compensation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gambit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A gambit in chess involves a player sacrificing material, usually a pawn, to gain a strategic advantage such as better positioning or initiative.
 
• The term "gambit" is derived from the Italian word "gambetto," meaning to trip someone.
 
• Common examples include the King’s Gambit and the Queen’s Gambit, which are well-known chess openings.
 
• Gambits can be accepted or declined by the opponent, leading to different lines of play.
 
• They are often used to surprise an opponent and force them into less familiar territory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **King’s Gambit**

 
 
• A historical chess opening starting with the moves 1.e4 e5 2.f4.
 
• It aims to control the center quickly and open lines for an aggressive attack.
 
• Popular during the 19th century, it is less common in modern high-level play due to its risky nature.
 
 
 
• **Queen’s Gambit**
 
 
• A classical chess opening starting with 1.d4 d5 2.c4.
 
• The objective is to offer the c4 pawn to gain a strong central presence.
 
• It is considered one of the most reliable and strategic openings in chess.
 
 
 
• **Accepted vs. Declined Gambits**
 
 
• In an accepted gambit, the opponent takes the offered material.
 
• In a declined gambit, the opponent avoids taking the material, instead focusing on other strategic goals.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Purpose**
 
 
• Gambits are used to disrupt the opponent’s plans and create dynamic positions.
 
• They often lead to complex and tactical middle games.

questions.question: How many players are there in a Field Hockey team?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __11__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Field hockey, also called hockey is an outdoor game played by two opposing teams of 11 players each.
 
• Players use sticks curved at the striking end to hit a small, hard ball into their opponent's goal.
 
• It is called field hockey to distinguish it from the similar game played on ice.
 
• Rules are made by the International Federation of Hockey. 
 
• The total duration of a field hockey match is 60 minutes. 
 
• It is played in four quarters of 15 minutes each.
 
• It consists of a goalkeeper and 10 field players.
 
• There are five substitutes on the bench and there is no limit to the number of times a player is allowed to be substituted.
 
• Apart from the length of the game, there are tied overtime of 5 minutes followed by a shootout.

questions.question: The term 'foot fault' is associated with which of the following games?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Tennis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"foot fault"** is primarily associated with the game of **tennis**.
 
• A **foot fault** occurs when a player steps on or over the baseline or into the wrong area while serving the ball.
 
• The rules regarding foot faults are outlined in the **International Tennis Federation (ITF) Rules of Tennis**.
 
• This rule ensures that the server does not gain an unfair advantage by stepping closer to the net during the serve.
 
• If a player commits a foot fault, the serve is considered a **fault**, and the player may lose a point if it is a repeated offense.
 
• Foot faults are monitored by the **line umpire**, who is positioned to observe the server's feet.
 
• The term emphasizes the importance of maintaining proper technique and adherence to the rules during a serve in tennis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hockey**__

 __
 
• The term **"foot fault"** is not associated with hockey.
 
• In hockey, players are prohibited from using their feet to stop or control the ball intentionally, but this is not referred to as a "foot fault."
 
• The game of hockey focuses on the use of a **stick** to maneuver the ball and score goals.
 
 
 
• **Archery**__
 __
 
• In archery, there is no term called **"foot fault."**
 
• However, archers must ensure their stance is within the boundaries of the designated shooting line while aiming and shooting.
 
• Archery relies on **precision, focus, and technique** rather than terms like foot faults.
 
 
 
• **Basketball**__
 
 
• The term **"foot fault"** does not apply to basketball.
 
• In basketball, there are specific violations such as **traveling, double dribbling,** and stepping out of bounds.
 
• Players may also commit a **"foot violation"** if they intentionally use their foot to kick the ball, but this is not referred to as a "foot fault."

questions.question: What is the standard length of a cricket pitch?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**22 yards**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A cricket pitch is a rectangular area located at the center of the field, measuring precisely **22 yards (20.12 meters) in length and 10 feet (3.05 meters) in width.**
 
• The pitch is used for bowling, batting, and running between the wickets during play.
 
• The length of 22 yards is internationally standardized by the **International Cricket Council (ICC).**
 
• The stumps are set at each end of the pitch, and the popping creases are marked 4 feet in front of the stumps.
 
• The pitch's dimensions have remained consistent since the early development of cricket in England in the 17th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology Related to Cricket Pitch:**

 
 
• **Crease:** Lines drawn on the pitch to define areas for the bowler and batsman.
 
• **Wicket:** Consists of three stumps and two bails, placed at each end of the pitch.
 
• **Popping Crease:** The line a batsman must reach to avoid being run out.
 
• **Bowling Crease:** The line where the stumps are placed.
 
 
 
• **Pitch Conditions:**
 
 
• Pitches can vary in nature—**flat pitches favor batsmen**, while grassy or cracked pitches benefit bowlers.
 
• In Test cricket, pitch conditions change significantly over five days, affecting gameplay.
 
 
 
• **Historical Development:**
 
 
• The 22-yard measurement has been in place since cricket's codification in the 18th century.
 
• It was derived from the traditional English unit of measurement called "chain," which equals 22 yards.
 
 
 
• **Role of ICC:**
 
 
• The ICC regulates pitch preparation to ensure consistency and fairness in international matches.
 
• Pitch inspections are conducted to avoid undue advantages for either batsmen or bowlers.

questions.question: In which sport is the term 'Dolphin Kick' commonly used?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swimming**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term 'Dolphin Kick' refers to a specific swimming technique primarily used in **competitive swimming**, especially in the butterfly stroke and underwater phases of other strokes.
 
• This kick involves a fluid, wave-like motion of the legs and hips, similar to the movement of a dolphin's tail.
 
• The 'Dolphin Kick' is considered one of the fastest ways to propel underwater and is often used during starts and turns in freestyle, backstroke, and butterfly events.
 
• Swimmers use core muscles to generate the wave motion, which starts at the hips and flows down to the feet for maximum propulsion.
 
• This technique plays a vital role in competitive swimming, as mastering it can lead to significant improvements in speed and performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Butterfly Stroke:**

 
 
• The butterfly stroke is one of the four main swimming strokes used in competitive swimming.
 
• It is characterized by a simultaneous movement of both arms in a circular motion and the use of the 'Dolphin Kick' for leg propulsion.
 
• This stroke requires a high level of coordination and strength, making it one of the most challenging swimming techniques.
 
 
 
• **Underwater Phase:**
 
 
• The underwater phase occurs immediately after a swimmer dives or completes a turn.
 
• During this phase, swimmers often use the 'Dolphin Kick' to maximize speed before surfacing.
 
• Rules in competitive swimming, such as FINA regulations, limit the distance swimmers can stay underwater to 15 meters after starts and turns.
 
 
 
• **Core Strength in Swimming:**
 
 
• Core strength is crucial for generating the wave-like motion required in the 'Dolphin Kick.'
 
• Strong abdominal and lower back muscles help swimmers maintain efficient and powerful movements.
 
• Exercises like planks and leg raises are commonly used to improve core strength among swimmers.
 
 
 
• **Competitive Swimming Rules:**
 
 
• FINA, the international governing body for swimming, establishes rules for strokes, starts, and turns in competitions.
 
• The 'Dolphin Kick' is regulated to ensure fair play, and swimmers must surface within 15 meters after starts or turns.
 
• Mastering the 'Dolphin Kick' while adhering to these rules can give swimmers a competitive edge.

questions.question: Scissor style and Western Roll are the techniques used in:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**High Jump**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Scissor Style** and **Western Roll** are classic techniques used in the **High Jump** event, which is part of **track and field sports.**
 
• The **Scissor Style** is one of the oldest techniques where the jumper runs at an angle and uses a scissor-like motion to clear the bar.
 
• The **Western Roll** involves approaching the bar diagonally, planting one foot, and rolling over the bar with the body facing down.
 
• These techniques were widely used before the advent of the **Fosbury Flop**, which revolutionized the high jump in the 1960s.
 
• The high jump is measured based on the height cleared by the jumper without displacing the bar.
 
• It is a key event in international competitions such as the **Olympics, World Athletics Championships,** and other regional athletic meets.
 
• Modern high jumpers use advanced techniques and training to optimize their performance, combining speed, flexibility, and strength.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Long Jump**__

 __
 
• The **Long Jump** is a track and field event where athletes attempt to leap as far as possible from a takeoff point.
 
• The technique primarily involves a strong run-up, a takeoff, flight, and landing.
 
• Notable techniques include the **hang style** and the **hitch-kick technique.**
 
• The event has different rules and measurement methods compared to the high jump.
 
 
 
• **Triple Jump**__
 __
 
• The **Triple Jump**, also known as the hop, step, and jump, is a track and field event.
 
• It involves three phases: a hop, a step, and a jump to maximize distance.
 
• The triple jump requires a unique approach and technique distinct from the high jump.
 
 
 
• **Pole Vault**__
 
 
• The **Pole Vault** is a track and field event where athletes use a pole to clear a high bar.
 
• This event involves specialized equipment and techniques, including planting the pole, swinging, and clearing the bar.
 
• Unlike the high jump, the pole vault incorporates the use of external tools (the pole) to achieve height.

questions.question: What does the term 'deuce' signify in tennis?

options.text: The final point in a game

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**A tied score at 40-40**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **tennis**, the term "**deuce**" signifies a tied score of **40-40** during a game.
 
• The scoring system in tennis progresses as **0 (love), 15, 30, and 40**. When both players reach 40, the score is tied and referred to as "**deuce**".
 
• At deuce, a player must win **two consecutive points** to secure the game.
 
• The first point after deuce is called "**advantage**" for the player who wins it. If the same player wins the next point, they win the game; if not, the score returns to deuce.
 
• The term "**deuce**" originates from the French word "**à deux**", meaning "**at two**", which refers to the two points needed to win the game.
 
• Deuce often leads to intense moments in tennis matches, as players need to demonstrate strong **mental focus** and **stamina** to win two consecutive points.
 
• This scoring system adds an element of excitement to the game, especially during critical stages of a match.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **A let**__

 __
 
• A "**let**" occurs during a serve if the ball touches the net but still lands in the correct service box.
 
• The serve is replayed in the case of a let, without penalty to the server.
 
• "Let" is a common occurrence in tennis, ensuring fairness in the game.
 
 
 
• **The final point in a game**__
 __
 
• The final point in a game is not specifically referred to as "**deuce**".
 
• Winning the final point depends on the scoring scenario, such as advantage or match point.
 
 
 
• **A fault in serving**__
 
 
• A "**fault**" occurs when the server fails to deliver the ball into the correct service box.
 
• If two consecutive faults occur, it is called a "**double fault**", and the opponent wins the point.
 
• Faults are common in tennis and players strive to avoid them to maintain their momentum.
